correctness.rationale: All n>=2 linearly admissible n-words avoiding 11 form arcs in a strongly connected directed overlap graph on admissible (n−1)-words, whose base arc count is F_(n+2). For each arc 0u0 with u avoiding 11 and containing 1, duplicate it: there are F_n−1, and a direct degree calculation gives in-degree = out-degree at each vertex; strong connectivity yields an Euler cycle whose periodic spelling is legal and covers every linear admissible window with claimed multiset. For lower bound, integer vertex potential phi = number of leading zeros before first one (or n−1 if none) obeys phi(tail)−phi(head)<=1 on every permissible arc and equals 1 on every duplicated arc. Subtracting one mandatory copy of each arc from arbitrary closed covering walk yields a nonnegative balanced corrective flow whose potential sum is F_n−1, proving at least that many extra traversals. This dual bound is unrestricted, not inferred from finite counts. Independently regenerated all allowed arcs, degree-balance and potential inequalities for n2..10; supplied check.py covers n2..17 and exhaustive shorter binary cycles n2..5.
residual_risks: Requires every linearly admissible length-n word, including 101 for n=3, despite periodic repetition of that word being inadmissible.
Does not classify all shortest words or alternate optimally repeated multisets.

value.rationale: Shortest cyclic superstrings representing every binary no-11 linear word are natural constrained universal-window objects, and the gap from impossible strict de Bruijn coverage demands an exact repeated-arc optimum. The result gives a complete all-n Fibonacci length, a concrete optimal cycle multiset, and a sharp combinatorial dual potential, useful as a benchmark for constrained sequence coverage beyond a finite census.
